summary: Mount Collins tower near Matachewan, Ontario: a 1937 radio installation is noted, and the cabin and tower were still standing in 2011.

events.note: An ultra-high frequency radio-telephone set was installed at the tower, per a Department of Lands and Forests report that the Canada Lookouts index cites.
Firelookout.ca record: observer's cabin and fire tower still standing, tower cab intact.

evidence.supports: index files the Mount Collins tower under the North Bay District
1937 radio-telephone set installed at the Mount Collins tower, citing the Department of Lands and Forests report
evidence.quote: 1937: A ultra-high frequency radio-telephone set was installed at the Mount Collins tower. (Report of the Department of Lands and Forests)

evidence.supports: index also has a RAYMOND entry placed at Mount Collins - Matachewan
in 2011 the observer's cabin and fire tower were still standing, the tower with its cab intact
evidence.quote: In 2011, both the observer's cabin and fire tower were still standing, the tower with its cab intact.

evidence.supports: Ontario towers came under the former Department of Lands and Forests, which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972
evidence.quote: They came under the jurisdiction of Ontario's former Department of Lands and Forests which became the Ministry of Natural Resources in 1972.

notes_for_editor: Unresolved naming: the Canada Lookouts index has a MOUNT COLLINS entry (North Bay District, with the 1937 radio note) and a RAYMOND entry at 'Mount Collins - Matachewan'. No source read says they are one tower, so the story says they may be and that the sources do not say. The Forest Rangers sentence is general to Ontario towers, not Mount Collins, and its site is undated. The brief's coordinates match the Firelookout.ca record to within about 15 m. No build date, height, design, staffing, access or current status beyond 2011 was found. The search budget was spent on the two discovery queries, so no further searches were run.
